Sodium bicarbonate acts as a buffer in the blood, increasing extracellular pH and buffering capacity. During intense exercise, hydrogen ions (H⁺) accumulate in muscle cells, contributing to fatigue. By increasing extracellular buffering, bicarbonate allows more hydrogen ions to move out of the muscle into the extracellular fluid, reducing intracellular acidosis and thereby improving performance.
